MODEL_FEEDBACK_JSON:
{
  "positive_alignment_reasons": [
    "The Sennheiser headphones connect with my earlier headset purchase, so the audio connection makes sense, although I would skip them without a replacement need or a stated microphone.",
    "The networking devices relate to my Wi-Fi and Ethernet adapters, so they recognize an area of interest, even though they do not address a need I have now."
  ],
  "negative_misalignment_reasons": [
    "The Echo Dot and Fire TV devices do not help with the practical computer connections reflected in my purchases, and I am not seeking voice assistance or TV streaming.",
    "My tablet mount purchase suggests an accessory for a tablet I already use, not a reason to buy another tablet.",
    "An Ethernet adapter serves a specific connection need; it does not establish that I have weak Wi-Fi coverage or need to replace my home network."
  ],
  "overgeneralized_signals": [
    "My interest in particular electronics seems to have been stretched into interest in many unrelated electronic devices.",
    "Buying accessories seems to have been taken as a reason to recommend larger devices or replacements, without evidence that I need them."
  ],
  "missing_or_underweighted_signals": [
    "My history centers on specific practical functions: adding USB ports, connecting displays, mounting an existing tablet, and getting an Ethernet connection.",
    "My purchases are spread over years, so an old headset or tablet accessory is weak evidence of a current shopping need.",
    "I rarely interact unless something fits a clear need; sharing a broad connection to electronics is not enough to make me choose it."
  ],
  "summary_diagnosis": "The recommendations recognized my interest in electronics but missed the specific accessory functions and current needs that drive my choices."
}
